concepts.title: Electric Current and Circuit
concepts.ncert_text: Electric current is expressed by the amount of charge flowing through a particular area in unit time. I = Q/t. SI unit is Ampere (A). Measured by Ammeter (series).

concepts.title: Electric Potential and Potential Difference
concepts.ncert_text: Work done to move a unit charge from one point to another. V = W/Q. SI unit is Volt (V). Measured by Voltmeter (parallel).

concepts.title: Ohm's Law
concepts.ncert_text: The potential difference V across the ends of a given metallic wire in an electric circuit is directly proportional to the current I flowing through it, provided its temperature remains the same. V = IR.

concepts.title: Factors on which Resistance Depends
concepts.ncert_text: Resistance R depends on length (l), area of cross-section (A), and nature of material. R = ρ(l/A). ρ is electrical resistivity (Ohm-metre).

concepts.title: Combination of Resistors
concepts.ncert_text: Series: Rs = R1 + R2 + R3. Parallel: 1/Rp = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + 1/R3.

concepts.title: Heating Effect of Electric Current
concepts.ncert_text: Heat produced in a resistor is H = I^2Rt (Joule's Law of Heating). Applications: Electric iron, heater, fuse.

concepts.title: Electric Power
concepts.ncert_text: The rate at which electric energy is dissipated or consumed. P = VI = I^2R = V^2/R. SI unit is Watt (W). Commercial unit: 1 kWh = 3.6 x 10^6 J.
